description:
MoviBot recommends a single movie from a curated 238-film Disney/Pixar catalog (feature films, 1940-2017) for requests that mix hard constraints with soft ones. It is a tool-calling agent: an LLM planner is given three tools and decides which the question actually needs. CatalogFilter answers from structured columns (year, genre, studio, spoken language, explicit title exclusions). PlotSearch answers from meaning, ranking films by semantic similarity over full plot synopses. SynopsisReader returns the full plot text so the planner can judge claims that no column encodes, such as whether a character dies or who betrays whom.

What it CAN do: combine structured and thematic constraints in one query; honour exclusions ("besides Frozen and Moana") as real filters rather than as omissions from the prose; verify story-level properties by reading the plot rather than guessing from genre; and explain why it rejected the obvious alternative.

What it CANNOT do: reason about films outside its catalog (it is a curated Disney/Pixar subset, not all of IMDb); it holds no cast or director data, so it cannot answer 'movies starring X'; 159 of 238 films are semantically searchable and 220 have readable plot text, so a query about one of the remaining films will fall back to structured facts only; and it does not stream or play content.

Two ranking guardrails are enforced in the data and tool code rather than in the prompt, so no plan can bypass them: shorts under 45 minutes are removed at data-preparation time (they carry very high ratings on very few votes and otherwise dominate every result), and ranking uses a vote-count-weighted Bayesian rating instead of the raw average.
purpose: Answer the kind of movie request that a filter alone cannot: one that combines facts the catalog stores with judgements only the story can settle, and return a single defensible recommendation with the reasoning shown.

prompt_template.template: Query: <a movie request in natural language. It may mix structured constraints (era, genre, studio, language, titles to exclude) with story-level ones (theme, tone, what must or must not happen in the plot, who it is for).>
prompt_template.example: Query: Best empowering princess movie besides Frozen and Moana.

architecture.notes: Module names here match the boxes in /api/model_architecture and the `module` field of every entry in the /api/execute steps trace. Tool calls are unmetered because all three tools run against local data; only the planner turns cost anything, which is what the turn bound exists to cap.

prompt_examples.prompt: Best empowering princess movie besides Frozen and Moana.
prompt_examples.expected_tool_path: Planner -> CatalogFilter(keywords=['princess','royalty'], exclude_titles=['Frozen','Moana'], require_synopsis=true) -> Planner -> Final Answer
prompt_examples.verified_tool_output: CatalogFilter matched 13 films, returned best-first by weighted rating: Mulan (1998, 7.42), Beauty and the Beast (1991, 7.38), Aladdin (1992, 7.31), Tangled (2010, 7.30), The Little Mermaid (1989, 7.06). Frozen and Moana are absent because the exclusion was applied as a filter, not left to the prose.
prompt_examples.status: Tool path verified locally at zero cost. The final natural-language response will be captured from the first real planner run once the LLM endpoint is enabled.

prompt_examples.prompt: Something safe for a toddler where nobody dies.
prompt_examples.expected_tool_path: Planner -> CatalogFilter(genres=['Animation'], require_synopsis=true) -> Planner -> SynopsisReader(top candidates) -> Planner -> Final Answer
prompt_examples.verified_tool_output: CatalogFilter matched 85 films; the top-rated are The Lion King (7.91), Inside Out (7.83), Up (7.73), WALL-E (7.73). SynopsisReader returned full plot text for the shortlist, which is the only way to establish that Mufasa dies in The Lion King and Ellie dies in Up while WALL-E has no deaths. Neither fact appears in any genre, keyword, or overview field.
prompt_examples.status: Tool path verified locally at zero cost. The final natural-language response will be captured from the first real planner run once the LLM endpoint is enabled.
